notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 9 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 7th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, up from 2% last season.

stakes: The Red Wings go in seventh in the Atlantic with 11 points, the Flames tied for sixth in the Pacific with 6 points.

CGY.head: A tough matchup for the Flames
CGY.body: Even though Calgary has home-ice advantage, Detroit has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flames can pull it off if they keep dangerous shots away.

DET.head: The Red Wings should have the upper hand
DET.body: Even though Calgary has home-ice advantage, Detroit has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flames can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

items.text: The Red Wings are newly without Daniil Tarasov, and have had to make do without Simon Edvinsson all season. John Gibson is expected to start.
Alex DeBrincat has a point in at least six straight games against Calgary, and 14 points in his last six against them.
The Flames are newly without Maxim Tsyplakov, and have been without Samuel Honzek, Joel Hanley and Connor Zary for several games.
The Flames have played better than their record (.333): their chances are worth about .444, and their goaltending has held them back.
